segments.text: Foods that I will never eat again as a food science major with a master's in agriculture.
People on this app are ruthless.
I don't think I've ever had so many hateful things said about me in such a short period of time.
I agree, people on TikTok can be kind of spicy, but compared to YouTube, you guys are mean.
I was preemptively blocked by this creator, but this video detailing this specific food,
she doesn't eat at the grocery store and explaining why your cereal is a spawn of Satan.
got six million views. And per her video I stitched, it didn't seem like her
message was received very well. Let's talk about why. To begin, videos where a
random person tells you the specific foods that they avoid at the grocery
store aren't really that helpful. I know it sounds callous, but I don't care.
Everyone has different dietary needs, food preferences, medical conditions,
cultural diets, food allergies, access to food, food budgets, and if she buys
Cheerios or not at the grocery store that doesn't affect any of those factors for me personally
That is until she starts spreading misinformation about Cheerios
Which may reach a vulnerable parent who feeds their toddler Cheerios because they're a shelf-stable cheap palatable source of iron
This is where we run into more trouble
Our other issue is that if you use an appeal to authority tactic to establish yourself as an expert like you have a food science and an agriculture
Agriculture degree when food science topics like the amount of glyphosate residues or
Agriculture topics like the carcinogenicity of glyphosate come up. You need to get your facts correct
And if you don't people might not be very happy
Granted, I don't know if glyphosate residues on Cheerios is more food science or food cam
But potato potato regardless we know that Cheerios do not have high amounts of glyphosate residues
This is a post by Food Science Babe from the Gram and when the EWG tested Cheerios for Glyphosate
residues, values measured at 833 parts per billion, which is significantly below EPA tolerance levels.
So, an 150 pound adult would have to eat over 5,000 cups a day for a prolonged period of time
for Glyphosate to become an issue. 5,000 cups every day, four months and months. Good luck with that.
Now, if someone has agriculture knowledge, this, my friends, is a no-brainer.
The Bayer lawsuit had to do with farmers using glyphosate in combination with other pesticides
for decades and inhaled. This had nothing to do with food. And when research actually
studied this further and looked at glyphosate independently, it wasn't significantly associated
with cancer at any site in a study of 54,000 people. And a look at 15 government agencies
and their consensus on glyphosate. Not genotoxic doesn't represent a risk of cancer.
not carcinogenic, not neurotoxic, et cetera.
So enjoy your Cheerios, even though Reese's Pups
are still better.
Okay, bye.
